summary.text: A field is a set on which addition, subtraction, multiplication and division are defined and behave as they do for rational numbers.
The best known fields are the rational, real and complex numbers, and others such as finite fields, p-adic fields and fields of rational functions are widely studied.
Any field can serve as the scalars of a vector space, which is the standard general setting for linear algebra.

facts.label: Short definition
facts.value: A commutative ring where 0 differs from 1 and nonzero elements have inverses

facts.label: Finite fields
facts.value: Used for error correction codes and cryptography

facts.label: Impossible constructions
facts.value: Field theory helps prove angle trisection and squaring the circle cannot be done

facts.label: Galois theory
facts.value: Gives a proof that general quintic equations cannot be solved in radicals

items.prompt: In a field you divide a by b. For which values of b is that allowed?

options.label: Any b at all, including zero
Any b that is not zero
Only b that are whole numbers

items.explain: Every nonzero element has a multiplicative inverse, and dividing means multiplying by it. Division by zero is excluded by definition.

items.prompt: A number system has addition, subtraction and multiplication, but some nonzero elements have no multiplicative inverse. Is it a field?

options.label: No, since addition must be missing
No, since every nonzero element needs an inverse

items.explain: The field axioms require a multiplicative inverse for each nonzero element, which is what makes division possible.

items.prompt: A field starts with only addition and multiplication plus inverses. How does it get subtraction a − b?

options.label: Add the additive inverse of b to a
Multiply a by the multiplicative inverse of b
Add the multiplicative inverse of b to a
Multiply a by the additive inverse of b

items.explain: Subtraction is defined as a − b = a + (−b), while division is a / b = a ⋅ b⁻¹.

items.prompt: You are doing linear algebra and need numbers to scale your vectors by. What can serve as those scalars?
items.explain: Any field may be used as the scalars for a vector space, the standard general context for linear algebra.

items.prompt: An engineer designs error correction codes and needs a field with finitely many elements. Which kind of field is used for this?
items.explain: Finite fields are used for error correction codes and cryptography, while function fields describe geometric objects and number fields are studied in number theory.

items.prompt: Complex numbers are drawn as arrows from the origin. You multiply two of them. What happens to the arrows' lengths and angles?
items.explain: Multiplying complex numbers combines rotating and scaling: you add the angles and multiply the lengths.
